topic: For every finite labelled causally sufficient linear Gaussian DAG with unrestricted positive noise variances and one coefficient per block of each target's parent partition, allowing singleton blocks, characterize equality of the full positive-definite covariance models. Prove that two blocked-colour states are equivalent exactly when they are connected by covered reversals whose reversed edge is a singleton block and whose endpoint partitions agree on their common parents, with the prescribed partition transport. Equivalently, prove the static criterion: common skeleton and unshielded colliders, identical nonsingleton parent-block families at every vertex, and fixed orientation for every edge joining vertices with unequal block families. Derive complete component enumeration, a shortest reversal path whose length is the number of disagreeing arrows, fixed-p generic Gaussian likelihood/BIC component recovery, and simultaneous inference for the component's finite causal-effect set. Do not broaden to unrestricted cross-target edge colourings or equate a compelled arrow with an identified coefficient. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Tangent supports at diagonal covariances recover each nonsingleton parent block; an exact sparse covariance separator forces every reversed edge to join equal endpoint block families; Chickering's monotone reversal theorem then supplies the proposed path. Exhaustive p=5 enumeration matched all 348631 states and 153462 static classes to move components, with exact separators and mixed-partition stress witnesses. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently audit tangent-support recovery and the arbitrary-reversed-edge sparse separator, especially extra target parents and simultaneous arrow changes, and verify the imported generic-faithfulness and monotone-transformation results. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the exact separator on legal five-node pairs and audit the monotone induction; any full-model-equivalent pair with different nonsingleton blocks or a reversal across unequal endpoint families falsifies the theorem. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_blocked_colour_reversal_complete.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The nearest coefficient-colouring result obtains singleton equivalence classes only by forbidding singleton coefficient blocks and explicitly leaves graphical and transformational equivalence open. Allowing singleton incoming blocks restores ordinary Markov-equivalent reversals, but a reversal also changes which target owns the coefficient, so skeletons and unshielded colliders alone do not determine whether the block restrictions define the same covariance image. The bounded scan found no result for the target-specific blocked-with-singletons subclass; the missing step is to prove that all and only compatible covered reversals preserve the coefficient-equality model under the required partition transport.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient theorem equating covariance-model equality with both a static skeleton/collider/nonsingleton-block-family criterion and connectivity by legal singleton-block covered reversals carrying an explicit partition-transport map.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames coefficient colours as causal communities, moves from covariance geometry to structural equivalence, and states the missing graphical and transformational layer directly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Equal incoming coefficients encode communities of direct causes -> excluding singleton communities yields structural identifiability -> admitting singleton communities creates a nontrivial equivalence class requiring a complete graphical and transformational characterization

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the monotone covered-reversal induction that selects a disagreeing arrow, reverses it without leaving the ordinary equivalence class, and decreases orientation disagreement by one.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired move graph is a restriction of the ordinary covered-reversal graph; the first changed proof step is showing that the selected reversal is singleton-block and partition compatible.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover equality-partition restrictions as covariance identities, determine the orientations they compel, and propagate those restrictions through an ordinary equivalence-class representation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest complete equivalence theorem for a partition-indexed restriction on linear Gaussian DAG parameters, although its partition constrains error variances rather than incoming coefficients.

method_exemplars.technique: Use target-local constrained regressions to compute the coloured Gaussian likelihood and its decomposable BIC score, then lift population equivalence to component-level model selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the likelihood and estimator machinery for precisely the same coefficient-coloured Gaussian model; only singleton-block quotienting is new.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the nonsingleton blocks in every target-specific parent partition are recoverable from the covariance-model tangent space at a diagonal covariance, despite extra parents and simultaneous orientation differences, or exhibit a smallest legal counterexample.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior GANM run proves partition rigidity only in empty-DAG and restricted parent-closed configurations, leaving arbitrary crossings and externally parented refinements open. The coloured-Gaussian literature supplies smoothness and fixed-graph rational parameter recovery, but those results assume the graph and parent sets are already known. Across competing orientations, a singleton edge support does not reveal its target, and an arbitrary reversed edge can coexist with extra parents and other reversed arrows. New work must prove that the minimal nonzero tangent supports canonically recover each repeated incoming block and then construct a sparse covariance witness whenever an endpoint partition would split such a block; otherwise a full-model-equivalent crossing counterexample defeats the proposed converse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A tangent-support and sparse-separator theorem recovering every nonsingleton parent block from the full covariance model under arbitrary extra parents and simultaneous arrow changes, or an explicit smallest positive-noise model-equivalent pair with different nonsingleton block families.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from rational parameter recovery to smooth model geometry is the natural setup for asking which first-order features survive when the coloured graph itself is unknown.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Coefficient equalities define smooth coloured Gaussian DAG submodels -> fixed-graph parameters are rationally recoverable -> equality of two model images should force first-order recovery of their nonsingleton incoming blocks

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate the trek-rule parametrization at a diagonal covariance and combine its block-generator supports with rational coefficient-identification constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired invariant is the tangent space of exactly the same coloured Gaussian DAG manifold; the new step is proving support invariance across different orientations and parent partitions.

method_exemplars.technique: Use equality-constrained Gaussian regression and the RDAG likelihood's linear-independence criteria to estimate the local covariance geometry and test the recovered block supports.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its constrained-regression geometry is the closest sample analogue of the population tangent directions whose support classes must be recovered.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a canonical, duplicate-free enumeration of each blocked-colour covariance-equivalence component and prove that its legal-reversal distance equals arrow Hamming distance, while separately enumerating distinct induced total-effect functionals.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Essential-graph and clique-tree algorithms encode fixed ordinary Markov-equivalence constraints, whereas a blocked-colour reversal transports a singleton block between endpoint partitions and its legality is evaluated in the current state. The prior subset-recursion and minimal-IDA proposals show how canonical states or functionals remove duplicates, but neither supplies path independence for transported partitions. The first changed step is a canonical state invariant proving that every legal reversal prefix leading to the same oriented graph yields the same partition state; without it, memoization can merge inequivalent states, and an arrow-Hamming shortest path alone does not yield duplicate-free or polynomial-delay enumeration.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A canonical finite component representation with a complete no-duplication enumeration algorithm and output-sensitive bound, a proof that shortest legal reversal length equals the number of disagreeing arrows, and a quotient enumerator emitting each distinct total-effect functional once.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates counting and enumeration as prerequisites for possible-effect analysis and organizes the problem around a canonical equivalence-class representation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational data identify an equivalence class rather than one DAG -> causal analysis requires traversing and counting its members -> transported coefficient partitions require a new canonical component representation and duplicate-free enumerator

method_exemplars.technique: Use a disagreement-decreasing covered-reversal induction in which every operation fixes one target arrow and never revisits it.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once every selected reversal is shown partition compatible, this proof architecture gives the desired arrow-Hamming geodesic.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose an essential graph into chordal components and count admissible moral acyclic orientations by clique-picking and minimal-separator recursion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination counts a constrained subset of ordinary MEC orientations; clique-prefix admissibility is the first step that must be replaced by partition-transport-compatible admissibility.

method_exemplars.technique: Attach recursive least-squares estimators and joint covariance calculations to the distinct causal-effect functionals returned by the enumerator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It turns equivalence-class enumeration into estimable total-effect outputs rather than stopping at a combinatorial list of DAG states.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish fixed-dimension generic Gaussian likelihood/BIC consistency for selecting the correct blocked-colour covariance-model component when singleton coefficient blocks give multiple state representations of the same model.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Smooth-model BIC theory compares a fixed list of model images, while ordinary GES theory works on score-equivalent Markov classes. Singleton blocked-colour states introduce several DAG-partition parametrizations of one covariance image, and inequivalent components can meet on zero-edge or coincident-block strata. The first transferred step is therefore to quotient exact likelihood ties, prove every lower- or equal-dimensional inequivalent image is separated from a generic true covariance by a positive Kullback–Leibler gap, and describe the excluded intersections as a proper algebraic set. The scan found coloured local scores and empirical GECS results, but no component-level consistency theorem for the singleton-allowing blocked class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem that, for fixed vertex count and parameters outside an explicit proper algebraic exceptional set, every global BIC minimizer lies in the true blocked-colour covariance-equivalence component with probability tending to one.

writing_exemplar.why: Its GECS section already supplies the causal-community motivation, target-local score, move types, and explicit consistency gap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Coefficient blocks make Gaussian scores target-local -> coloured search is computationally feasible but lacks consistency theory -> singleton blocks change the statistical target from one identifiable DAG to an equivalence component

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Laplace expansion and dimension penalties for finitely many smooth curved exponential-family submodels, separating misspecified models by likelihood loss and overfitted models by BIC penalty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Coloured Gaussian DAG images are smooth covariance submanifolds; the changed step is grouping equal images and proving generic separation from every inequivalent component.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine local consistency of a decomposable score with a monotone graph-transformation theorem to show that greedy search reaches the optimal equivalence class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the template for a later algorithmic rung, where ordinary equivalence classes and moves are replaced by blocked-colour components and partition-aware transformations.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop simultaneous, selection-aware inference for the finite set of total causal effects induced by all states in a recovered blocked-colour covariance-equivalence component, including coincident-effect regimes.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A singleton-block component may contain observationally identical DAGs with different total effects, so the population target is a finite set rather than one graph-indexed coefficient. IDA supplies possible values but not joint confidence regions, and existing post-discovery methods target one true effect or an identifiable equal-variance graph. The failed in-repo IDA proposal identifies the additional missing certificate: the graph screen and duplicate-effect partition must be derived, not assumed. New work must combine component selection, the joint delta or bootstrap law of all member-labelled regression/path functionals, and a collision-safe representation that does not rely on regular matching of nearly equal effect values.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A component-aware estimator with a joint Gaussian or bootstrap limit and a simultaneous confidence region covering every distinct effect in the finite set after component selection, with explicit validity conditions for duplicate or locally colliding effects.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly separates graph-selection uncertainty from coefficient uncertainty and explains why graph-first plug-in intervals target the wrong object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal effects depend on an unknown graph -> reusing discovery data invalidates naïve intervals -> blocked-colour observational equivalence makes the target a whole finite effect set -> inference must cover its members simultaneously

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate possible parent sets locally and map each to a regression functional for the total effect, retaining the distinct possible values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The blocked-colour component likewise induces finitely many graph-specific regression functionals, with legal parent sets further restricted by transported coefficient partitions.

method_exemplars.technique: Resample discovery statistics, screen candidate graphs, form graph-specific effect intervals, and aggregate them while proving coverage after selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its screening-and-aggregation proof directly handles reuse of discovery data; the changed step is familywise coverage of every value in an unordered component-level effect set.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert goodness-of-fit tests jointly over structural and numerical parameters to construct total-effect regions incorporating graph uncertainty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Blocked coefficient equalities are smooth Gaussian restrictions amenable to test inversion, but the null must range over an equivalence component and return a set-valued effect region.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-p generic BIC consistency deliberately removes the contiguous regimes where distinct blocked covariance-model strata meet. The covariance-shift run leaves the bounded-information power envelope open, while the SCORE run records that a two-point Chernoff calculation did not produce an attaining learner. In the blocked-colour setting the obstacle is composite singular geometry: zero edges and coincident coefficients create intersecting covariance varieties, and the component label changes discontinuously across their tangent cones. The first proof step must therefore derive a local Gaussian experiment for competing tangent cones rather than apply a regular within-model likelihood expansion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A tangent-cone Gaussian experiment at each blocked-model collision, an explicit minimax correct-classification or honest-abstention envelope indexed by local information distance, and a likelihood- or score-based component selector attaining that envelope.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates honest structural uncertainty rather than treating the selected causal graph as certain, providing the right arc for a local nonidentification boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Population restrictions distinguish causal structures -> the distinguishing signal may shrink at the sampling scale -> generic consistency gives no protection at model intersections -> derive the optimal local certification or abstention envelope

method_exemplars.technique: Relate optimal testing error to likelihood-ratio information and expand it along least-favourable local paths joining competing structural strata.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Component recovery is a finite composite testing problem whose two-stratum restrictions reduce to Chernoff testing.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert structural goodness-of-fit tests to obtain honest recovery sets instead of conditioning inference on a deterministically selected graph.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An attaining procedure must remain valid at component intersections where deterministic correct selection is impossible.

literature_map:
Verma and Pearl (1990, UAI) give the classical same-skeleton/same-v-structure criterion for ordinary DAG Markov equivalence.
Chickering (1995, UAI) gives the corresponding covered-reversal transformation and an arrow-disagreement-length path.
Andersson, Madigan, and Perlman (1997, Annals of Statistics) represent ordinary equivalence classes by unique essential graphs with chordal chain components.
Makam, Reichenbach, and Seigal (2023, Electronic Journal of Statistics; arXiv:2108.10058) analyze coefficient-equality RDAG models and constrained Gaussian likelihood geometry.
Wu and Drton (2023, IEEE JSAIT; arXiv:2308.08959) characterize equivalence under partial equality of error variances and construct its CPDAG representation.
Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus (2026, JRSSB; arXiv:2404.04024) establish rational Markov properties, smooth geometry, generic edge-colour faithfulness, BPEC identifiability, and GECS.
Boege et al. exclude singleton blocks from BPEC identifiability and explicitly leave graphical and transformational coloured-DAG equivalence open.
The same paper leaves consistency of GECS open; its empirical evidence and decomposable BIC do not yet give component recovery for singleton-allowing blocks.
Haughton (1988, Annals of Statistics) supplies BIC asymptotics for finite smooth curved exponential-family models, matching the local geometry but not the quotient by equal covariance images.
Chickering (2002, JMLR) supplies the local-score plus monotone-transformation architecture behind ordinary GES consistency.
Wienöbst, Bannach, and Liśkiewicz (2023, JMLR; arXiv:2205.02654) count and sample ordinary MECs by clique-picking and connect multiplicity to possible-effect analysis.
Wienöbst, Luttermann, Bannach, and Liśkiewicz (2023, AAAI; arXiv:2301.12212) give linear-delay MEC enumeration with fixed background knowledge, not transported partitions.
Maathuis, Kalisch, and Bühlmann (2009, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:0810.4214) consistently estimate possible effects across an ordinary MEC without simultaneous confidence regions.
Strieder and Drton (2023, JCI; arXiv:2309.04298) and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2026, Biometrika; arXiv:2405.06763) address structure-aware effect inference, but neither covers a full blocked-colour finite effect set.
